content.overview: A contingent contract is a contract to do or not to do something if some event collateral to the contract does or does not happen. Enforcement depends on the event under ss. 32–36.

sections.heading: Structure
sections.body: Identify the collateral event. Contingent contracts cannot be enforced until the event happens (s. 32); if the event becomes impossible, the contract becomes void.

sections.heading: Track B
sections.body: Plead the contingency and its occurrence or failure. Distinguish conditions precedent from ordinary promises.
